§3.1 Elements

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

output-elements · output output-model layout

✅ Normative

A document is represented as a sequence of pages, each a sequence of elements in reading order. Every element MUST have exactly one class from the table below and MUST be rendered in Markdown as that class prescribes.

An element is the smallest unit the protocol reasons about: it has one class, one rendering, one position in reading order and — when boxes are requested — one box. The classes are the layout classes of Block Classes§5.3; the rendering column says how each appears in the Markdown. An element's class MUST be identical in its layout annotation and its Markdown representation. Its Markdown syntax MAY be shared by several classes; the element's role determines the class.

Class Rendering in Markdown Defined in
Title ATX heading at the document's top level Document Type§4.4, Heading Depth Across Pages§4.5
Section-header ATX heading (#…######) at its document depth Heading Depth Across Pages§4.5, Recognising Ambiguous Headings§6.7
Text Paragraph; inline marks per Text Formatting Conventions§7.1 chapter 7
List-item Markdown list item, nesting by printed indentation Bullets and Sub-Bullets§8.1
Table HTML <table> chapter 9
Caption For a table or chart, <caption> first or last inside its table HTML according to reading order; otherwise a paragraph adjacent to its object Titles Banners Captions§9.7.3
Footnote Paragraph at its printed position Footnotes Inside the Frame§9.7.2
Formula $$ … $$ LaTeX, with its printed equation number Displayed Equations§7.2.2
Picture Its content as text: a chart table (<table data-source="chart">), a diagram/<language> block, a description fallback block, or a prose description Images and Figures§12.1.2
Code Fenced code block Block Classes§5.3
Page-header / Page-footer Its own block, never a heading Recurring Page Furniture§4.6, Markdown Rendering§3.2
Form / Key-Value Region Key-value lines with [blank] for empty fields chapter 10
Checkbox-Selected / -Unselected [x] / [ ] before its label Checkboxes§10.4.2
Document Index Nested list, label then page number Table of Contents§6.10

Elements inside elements

A table contains cells; a list contains items; a form contains fields. These inner elements are rendered inside their parent's Markdown and receive boxes only at the granularity that was requested — see Boxes and Granularity§3.3.

A table or chart caption is rendered inside its object's <table> but retains the Caption class and its own layout box. HTML nesting does not merge the caption into the Table or Picture class.

Content outside the reading flow

Watermarks, margin banners, stamps, seals, handwriting and sidenotes are elements too. Each has a defined place in the Markdown even though it sits outside the body flow on the page — see Watermarks§7.3.13, Margin Banners§7.3.5, Seals and Round Stamps§7.3.9, Handwritten Annotations§7.3.3 and Marginal Notes§6.4.
